issues.display_title: Issue #41: fix(upload): Reupload keeps failing after a signal drop even when the connection is back
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

When an upload loses signal partway through, the project ends in the Upload Failed — N image(s) failed to upload state. Pressing Reupload (N) after the connection is back to normal still fails, and nothing is uploaded. The card only shows the generic "Upload Failed" message, so the user cannot tell why.

Observed on project Crop (1799 frames, GPS mode, 5 ft spacing): 13 frames uploaded, 4 failed (1549, 1611, 1673, 1797). Reupload never recovered.

Root Cause

The reupload job stops at its first step, check_upload_permission. The manifest supports this:

  • upload.status stays partial. Step 2 of run_upload would have written uploading if the job had got that far.
  • The frame files keep their original mtime. Step 5, the EXIF re-tag, never ran.

The permission check, get_upload_token and create_tour all use the shared GothruClient HTTP client (crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs). That client was built with no timeout and with the default keep-alive connection pool. When the signal drops, the pool keeps dead sockets. The next request reuses one of them and either errors or hangs, even though the network has recovered.

The frame upload loop already uses its own client with timeouts, so it was not affected.

In addition, the failed job event carries an error string, but uploadStore discards it and shows only the generic failed_upload text.

Changes Made

  • crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs: GothruClient now sets pool_max_idle_per_host(0) (a fresh connection per request), connect_timeout(15s) and timeout(60s). These calls are few, so the extra TLS handshakes cost little.
  • src/features/upload/model/uploadStore.ts: on a failed event, show a danger toast with event.error so the real cause (network, permission or token) is visible.

Verification

  • Start an upload, cut the network mid-upload, and wait for the partial state.
  • Restore the network and press Reupload. The failed frames upload and the status becomes complete.
  • Force a failure (e.g. keep the network off and press Reupload). A toast shows the actual error, and the job does not hang indefinitely.
  • cargo test -p sb-core: the gothru tests pass. Two unrelated project::store path-normalization tests fail; these were not caused by this change.
  • The frontend typecheck and pnpm test pass (102 tests).

issues.display_title: Issue #42: fix(projects): Project order keeps changing on the Upload page and sidebar
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-09-24.at.14.23.20.mov

Description

With several projects in the list, the order of the project cards on the Upload page keeps changing. The project list in the sidebar also reorders: clicking a project in the sidebar moves it to the top, so every card shifts position.

Root Cause

The recent-projects index (recent-projects.json) decides the order of the sidebar, the Home carousel and the Upload page. Three code paths moved a project to the front of that index:

  • UploadView called commands.openProject for every recent project only to read its manifest. open_project also moves the project to the front of the index. These calls run in parallel and finish in random order, so the saved order was shuffled every time the Upload page mounted. The next fetchRecent() then read the shuffled order. fetchRecent() runs after an upload, a selection change or a tour-details save.
  • project::update, which is shared by rename, selection, tour details and view updates, moved the edited project to the front. Editing a card on the Upload page made that card jump to the top.
  • project::open_project, called when a project is clicked in the sidebar, moved the clicked project to the front.

Changes Made

  • crates/sb-core/src/project/store.rs: new refresh_recent, which updates an existing entry in place and keeps its position. upsert_recent (move to front) is now used only by create_project. Both share a private write_recent.
  • crates/sb-core/src/project/mod.rs: open_project and update use refresh_recent. New read-only read_project.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/projects.rs, src-tauri/src/lib.rs: new read_project command. It reads the manifest and authorises the asset directory without touching the recent index.
  • src/shared/api/commands.ts: commands.readProject.
  • src/features/upload/components/UploadView.tsx: load manifests with readProject instead of openProject.

The project order is now stable everywhere. It changes only when a new project is created, and new projects are added at the top.

Side effects:

  • Renaming a project no longer moves it to the top.
  • After login, the app auto-opens recent[0]. This is now the most recently created project, not the most recently opened one.

Verification

  • With 3 or more projects, open the Upload page several times. The card order stays the same.
  • Change the selection settings or tour details on a card that is not first. The card keeps its position.
  • Click different projects in the sidebar. The sidebar and Upload order do not change.
  • Create a new project. It appears at the top.
  • cargo test -p sb-core project: recent_index_upsert_dedups_and_orders now also checks that refresh_recent keeps the position. Two project::store path-normalization tests fail for reasons unrelated to this change (Windows paths on macOS). They also fail without it.
  • cargo clippy --workspace, pnpm build and pnpm test (102 tests) pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #43: fix(network): Show human-readable messages instead of raw HTTP errors
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Description

Error messages from HTTP requests reach the user in technical form. A wrong email or password on the login screen shows HTTP 404: There is no user found with this username and password. Other failures show text such as HTTP 500, creating tour: error sending request for url (...) or Upload token unavailable. The status codes, URLs and internal step names mean nothing to the user.

Root Cause

Every HTTP error became an SbError::Network(String) built from technical data, and the frontend (parseErrorMessage) displays detail as it is:

  • parse_json in crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs formatted error responses as HTTP {status}: {detail}, or as HTTP {status} when the body had no JSON message.
  • Transport errors (no connection, timeout, a dropped connection) used reqwest::Error::to_string(). That text includes the URL and the OS error. Several call sites also added an internal prefix, for example creating tour:, lookup place: or uploading frame:.
  • A response body with an unexpected shape produced unexpected response shape: <serde error>.

Changes Made

  • crates/sb-core/src/gothru/mod.rs
    • When the server sends a readable message, only that message is shown, without the HTTP xxx: prefix.
    • status_message(status): human text for an error status that has no server message. It covers 400, 403, 404, 408/504, 429, 5xx, and a generic fallback for anything else. 401 still maps to Unauthenticated.
    • net(e) is now pub(crate). It maps reqwest errors to human text for timeout, connection, decode and other failures. The raw error goes to the log through tracing::warn!.
    • A response with an unexpected shape now shows a human message. The serde error is logged.
  • auth/google.rs, upload/tour.rs, upload/places.rs, upload/queue.rs: all reqwest map_err calls go through gothru::net. The messages empty moderation_id returned and Upload token unavailable are rewritten in plain language.

Example messages:

Case Before After
Wrong login HTTP 404: There is no user found… There is no user found with this username and password
Server 500 HTML page HTTP 500 The server is having a problem. Please try again later.
Offline creating tour: error sending request for url (…) Could not reach the server. Check your internet connection and try again.
Timeout … operation timed out The server took too long to respond. Please try again.

Verification

  • Sign in with a wrong email or password. The error has no HTTP 404: prefix.
  • Turn off the network and try to sign in or upload. A human "Could not reach the server…" message appears.
  • Sign in with correct credentials, and complete an upload. Both work as before.
  • cargo test -p sb-core: 126 passed. The 5xx HTML test now checks for the human message, and the upload-token test checks for the new text. Two project::store path-normalization tests fail for reasons unrelated to this change (Windows paths on macOS).
  • cargo clippy --workspace passes with no warnings.

issues.display_title: Issue #44: fix(bundle): Windows installer shows the default NSIS icon instead of the app logo
issues.main_description_html:
Description

The Windows installer (Gothru Street Builder_2.0.2_x64-setup.exe) shows the default NSIS icon in place of the GoThru app logo. The uninstaller also shows the default icon.

Root Cause

bundle.windows.nsis.installerIcon is not set in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json. When this value is missing, Tauri uses the default NSIS icon for the setup .exe. The bundle.icon list controls only the app executable, the window, the taskbar and the macOS bundle. It does not control the installer icon.

Changes Made

  • src-tauri/tauri.conf.json: add bundle.windows.nsis.installerIcon: "icons/icon.ico". The installer and the uninstaller now use the app logo.
"windows": {
  "nsis": {
    "installerIcon": "icons/icon.ico"
  }
}

Other Icons Checked

Item Status
src-tauri/icons/* (png, icon.ico 16–256 px, icon.icns) Already the GoThru logo
App .exe, window, taskbar Correct (from bundle.icon)
macOS .app / DMG Correct (from icon.icns)
NSIS installer / uninstaller Fixed by this change
NSIS header image / sidebar image Still the NSIS default. Optional: needs a 150×57 header BMP and a 164×314 sidebar BMP

Verification

  • cargo check passes (config validated by tauri-build)
  • Build the Windows installer and confirm the setup .exe and the uninstaller show the GoThru logo
